- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.5) and understate when sentiment is negative (especially <0.0).
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in price — model tends to overreact and peak too early.
- Underestimate in the first 5–7 days of a new trend if sentiment is bullish (model lags sentiment shift).
- Overestimate in the final 5–7 days of a trend if sentiment is bearish (model fails to correct downward).
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after sustained upward moves, especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit recent noise and misjudge direction.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often underestimates late-period volatility — especially when sentiment turns negative mid-horizon.
